newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary starts probe of farm export subsidy usage.
newsitem.headline: Hungary starts probe of farm export subsidy usage.

text.p: Hungary has started a crackdown on the abuse of agricultural subsidies and plans to change the system in the near future, a government official said on Monday.
"We hope to have at least an idea about the extent of possible frauds by the time our investigation is finished," Sandor Rubicsek, head of the Government Investigative Office (KEI) told Reuters.
"We would like to review the entire procedure and find ways to make it more transparent and more efficient".
The daily newspaper Vilaggazdasag reported on Monday that the police have started inquiries into several cases of suspected fraud involving agricultural export subsidies.
It also said that according to Tax Office figures, irregular use of those subsidies amounted to 5.2 billion forints last year and 5.4 billion in 1995.
Frauds included the repeated export of the same shipments, fictitious exports and claiming subsidies for other product categories than those actually exported.

The Agriculture Ministry plans to spend 100 billion forints on farming subsidies and regional development this year, and minister Frigyes Nagy said earlier they plan to change the subsidy system over the next few years.
He also said this year's subsidy regulations were already stricter and better targeted than previous ones.
Rubicsek said the KEI does not plan to look into earlier usage of farming subsidies but he expects some information to surface anyway.
He added that their investigation will last until the end of May.
